answer: Bind each identity to one carrier-issued SIM or eSIM: the carrier attests the SIM's unique IMSI, locks the number against porting 90 days, and requires Play Integrity or App Attest, so a hollow emulator image fails. A registration pulse from the carrier confirms the number is live and billed, while a plume of porting requests from one device flags a farm. An attacker pays about $10-$30 per SIM plus a monthly plan, so cost scales linearly per fake identity. Limits: dual-SIM phones, prepaid churn, and users without a mobile plan need another path; re-attest randomly each epoch.
